target: arousal/activation distinction (EEG-level operationalization)
note: The paper's core theoretical contribution: separates 'arousal' (current energetic level, global/topography-flat) from 'activation' (task-related energy mobilization, topographically-focal), operationalizing Pribram and McGuinness's (1975) attention-system distinction at the EEG level for the first time (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2765-2766).

target: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
note: Analogical only, not the authors' framing: the eyes-open visual-fixation/processing condition loosely parallels an 'engaged' state relative to passive eyes-closed rest; offered to meet this strand's mandatory treats-construct requirement honestly given the source never discusses engagement or boredom (P/anticipatory-application).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
note: Analogical only: eyes-closed rest (no external target, no visual-processing demand) is the paper's closest physiological analogue to reduced external engagement; the source itself never characterizes eyes-closed rest this way (P/anticipatory-application).

target: EEG eyes-open vs. eyes-closed
note: Central paradigm: 32 min alternating 2-min eyes-closed/eyes-open blocks, 'triplet' order-controlled design, 19-site 10-20 system, N=28; global power reductions in all 4 bands with eyes-open, differential topographic patterns per band (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2767-2771).

target: EEG alpha/theta power
note: Absolute power via FFT (Welch window); alpha = global arousal marker (uniform ~40% reduction, tracks SCL); theta = activation marker (global reduction, significantly larger posteriorly) (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2768-2771).

target: heart rate / HRV (+ skin conductance)
note: Skin conductance level (SCL) continuous at 64Hz from non-dominant-hand digit electrodes; increases eyes-closed to eyes-open (F=5.53, p<.05); negatively correlated with alpha at 2 of 3 eyes-closed periods and with the alpha change score (r=-.32) (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2767, 2769, 2771).

target: arousal (current energetic level) <- EEG alpha power (global)
note: The paper's own internal construct-measure pairing: arousal is operationalized via alpha power's uniform, non-topographic, SCL-tracking reduction (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2770-2771).

target: activation (task-related energy mobilization) <- EEG topographic delta/theta/beta changes
note: The paper's own internal construct-measure pairing: activation is operationalized via regionally-focal (non-uniform) changes in delta, theta, and beta power (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2769-2771).

target: Berger, H. (1933); Adrian, E.D., & Matthews, B.H.C. (1934); Jasper, H.H. (1936); Smith, J.R. (1938)
note: Foundational discovery lineage of occipital alpha suppression with visual stimulation/eye-opening, the phenomenon this paper decomposes into arousal and activation components (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2765).

target: Volavka, J., Matousek, M., & Roubicek, J. (1967); Gale, A., Coles, M., & Boyd, E. (1971)
note: Proponents of the Reticular Activating System (RAS) mediation account of alpha desynchronization to visual input (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2765-2766).

target: Gevins, A., Smith, M.E., McEvoy, L., & Yu, D. (1997); Basar, E., & Schurmann, M. (1999); Klimesch, W. (1999)
note: Proponents of the widespread thalamo-cortical communication account of alpha desynchronization, the rival mechanistic account to RAS mediation (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766).

target: Barry, R.J., Clarke, A.R., McCarthy, R., Selikowitz, M., Rushby, J.A. (2005a)
note: Extends the CPT study's arousal/activation distinction (previously demonstrated via SCL and behavioral efficiency) into the domain of EEG topography, not examined in the earlier paper (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766).

target: Barry, R.J., Rushby, J.A., Wallace, M.J., Clarke, A.R., Johnstone, S.J., Ilinka, Z. (2005b)
note: Extends the caffeine study's use of absolute (not relative) EEG power and global-alpha/SCL arousal linkage into a topographic, multi-band eyes-closed/eyes-open design (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766, 2768).

target: Barry, R.J., Clarke, A.R., McCarthy, R., Selikowitz, M., Rushby, J.A., Ploskova, E. (2004)
note: Prior study in children linking SCL to global (non-topographic) EEG alpha reduction; direct empirical precedent this study replicates on a between-subjects basis in adults (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766, 2769).

target: VaezMousavi, S.M., Barry, R.J., Rushby, J.A., Clarke, A.R. (2007)
note: Independent between-subjects confirmation of the arousal/activation separation in normal adults, cited as converging evidence for the theoretical framework this paper extends (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766).

target: McCarthy, Gregory, & Wood, Charles C. (1985)
note: Source of the vector-scaling correction applied to confirm that reported condition-by-topography interactions are genuine and not scaling artifacts (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2768).

target: Detari, L. (2000); Robbins, T., Granon, S., Muir, J., Durantou, F., Harrison, A., Everitt, B. (1998)
note: Neuroanatomical grounding for thalamic/midbrain mediation of arousal and its propagation to cortical EEG activity, cited to justify the expectation that arousal changes should appear globally across the scalp (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766).

target: Ray, W.J., & Cole, H.W. (1985)
note: Cited to interpret the eyes-open frontal beta increase as consistent with prior findings that beta reflects emotional/cognitive processing and mental/physical effort (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2772).

target: classic alpha-desynchronization literature (Berger 1933 onward, treating visual-stimulation alpha suppression as unitary 'cortical activation')
note: Qualifies the earlier literature's unitary reading by showing the alpha reduction it documents is a pure global-arousal effect, distinct from the topographically-focal activation effects visible in delta, theta, and beta (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2771).

target: eyes-closed/eyes-open baseline-equivalence assumption in EEG and ERP methodology
note: Reframes the field's implicit assumption that eyes-closed and eyes-open rest are interchangeable 'lowest-arousal' baselines, proposing instead that baseline choice should depend on whether the target task involves visual processing or a fixation point (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2771-2772).

target: Reticular Activating System (RAS) mediation vs. thalamo-cortical widespread-communication debate on alpha desynchronization mechanism
note: Does not adjudicate the mechanism debate directly but reframes it: the global SCL-tracking alpha component is consistent with RAS-style arousal mediation, while topographically-focal delta/theta/beta changes are consistent with thalamo-cortical processing, suggesting the two mechanisms may co-occur rather than compete (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2765-2766, 2771).

target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study): EEG eyes-open/eyes-closed baseline channel
note: ****** UNVERIFIED: this paper's finding that eyes-closed and eyes-open rest differ in both global arousal and topographic activation is the normative methodological citation for choosing/interpreting any resting-state EEG baseline channel the not-yet-built VR Attention Study dataset might collect; dataset entry does not exist on disk (P/anticipatory-application).

target: Part III methodological caution for any future physiological/EEG baseline measure
note: P/anticipatory-application -- should Part III's research program ever incorporate a physiological baseline (directly, or via the linked VR Attention Study dataset), this paper is the citation for why eyes-closed and eyes-open resting periods cannot be treated as interchangeable zero-points.

target: Strand D internal corpus-architecture note (baseline-methodology prerequisite for bor-sec-30 and bor-sec-33)
note: P/anticipatory-application -- our own observation, not a claim made by later papers: bor-sec-30 (Perone et al., frontal EEG asymmetry across a boring task) and bor-sec-33 (Yuvaraj et al., EEG functional connectivity during boredom) each inherit an obligation to justify their resting/inter-block baseline choice given this paper's topographic findings, though neither paper cites Barry et al. (2007) directly (this paper predates neither by citation but the two later units' own reference lists should be checked independently).

target: Fisch, B.J. (1999) -- EEG primer
note: Cited as acknowledging that the underlying mechanism of alpha desynchronization to visual input remains unclear, framing the mechanistic debate this paper's arousal/activation decomposition partially addresses (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2765-2766).

target: Pribram, Karl H., & McGuinness, Donald (1975)
note: Originators of the arousal/activation/effort tripartite distinction as separable processes of the attention system; the paper's foundational theoretical premise, previously underused in psychophysiological research per the authors (FAITHFUL-Barry et al., ~p.2766).
